prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down workspace where the floor sits roughly 0.8 to 1.0 metres below the downward-looking camera wearer, containing three circular metal platters within arm's reach (0.2 to 0.4 metres apart from one another): a large foreground platter with yellow mixture at the bottom-center (~0.7 metres away), an upper-center platter with shaped dumplings and tongs (~0.9 metres away), and a middle-right bowl with white dough (~0.8 metres away). To the left (~0.3 to 0.6 metres from the camera wearer), a person seated in red clothing extends both arms rightward over the workspace, while a second person's hands are partially visible at the top-right edge (~1.0 metre away), with both people's heads and faces completely out of view outside the frame so neither is seen looking toward the camera wearer. Across the five frames, the left person's brighter foreground right arm reaches across to the right dough bowl in frame 1 (occluding the middle of the scene at ~0.3 to 0.4 metres depth), retracts leftward and lowers in frames 2 and 3 while their left hand rises higher and closer (~0.4 metres), and then both hands converge above the left rim of the foreground platter at ~0.5 metres in frames 4 and 5. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the vertical height of the left person's overlapping arms above the floor platters despite dark cast shadows in the dim lighting, and reveals the concave depth profile inside the bowls. However, the depth map is unreliable around the top-left stove fire and upper background wall, which collapse into flat black regions with lost surface geometry, and it slightly blurs the boundary between the left person's lower arm and their knee in frame 2.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map delineates the two-dimensional footprints and boundaries of the three circular floor platters (~0.7 to 0.9 metres from the camera wearer and ~0.2 to 0.4 metres apart) and the adjacent people within arm's reach of the food containers, though all heads and torsos remain partly out of view at the left and top-right frame edges facing inward toward the workspace rather than toward the camera wearer. In frame 1, the left person's extended right arm (~0.3 to 0.5 metres away) creates a large contiguous mask that stretches rightward across the frame and partially occludes the foreground platter below it and the upper platter behind it, before retracting leftward across frames 2 through 5 so that all three circular platters become fully unoccluded on the right side of the workspace. The map also captures the second person at the top-right (~1.0 metre away, ~0.5 metres behind the right bowl) in frame 2 and tracks the left person's two arms merging into a single region to the left of the foreground platter in frames 3 to 5. What segmentation makes clearer than RGB is the crisp outer boundary of the shadowed metal platters and the exact spatial extent of the left person's body and arms against the similarly dark background floor. However, the map is semantically and spatially unreliable in several places: in frame 1 it misses the upper and right bowls entirely while mislabelling the person's arm and the foreground mixture as 'pizza' and sleeve as 'broccoli', in frames 4 and 5 holes appear inside the left person's shadowed lower arm mask, and the background floor is inconsistently labelled as 'dining table' or dropped into black background.
descriptions.pose: The skeleton map isolates hand and arm joint geometry against a black background, showing only the left person's left hand in the middle-left (~0.4 to 0.6 metres from the camera wearer) while all other body parts, faces, and the second person at the top-right (~1.0 metre away) are unrendered and out of view, confirming no visible face is oriented toward the camera wearer. Across the 5 frames, the tracked magenta left hand starts lower on the left in frame 1 (partially occluded from above by the unrendered reaching right arm at ~0.3 metres), rises upward and slightly closer to the camera wearer in frame 2 as the right arm retreats, moves slightly downward and rightward in frame 3, and settles near the left edge of the foreground platter (~0.5 metres away, within arm's reach of both the camera wearer and the platters) in frames 4 and 5. In frames 3 and 4, yellow arm/body keypoints briefly appear below the magenta hand, tracing the forearm and lower-arm segment extending down toward the bottom-left corner (~0.5 to 0.6 metres away). Compared to the RGB strip, the pose map precisely reveals the 3D finger articulation and curling of the left person's left hand as it pinches a dough ball across the sequence, even against skin-toned and shadowed backgrounds. However, the pose map is highly incomplete and unreliable for full-scene understanding: it completely fails to detect the left person's foreground right arm and hand across all five frames (even when fully visible in frames 1, 4, and 5), misses the top-right person's hands entirely, and produces hallucinated or misaligned yellow body/torso struts on the left arm in frames 3 and 4.
